scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

First, the parent noticed that their daughter was taking more money than usual for lunch. They planted a $20 bill to catch her, and when she took it, they called the police. The intention was to teach the daughter a lesson about stealing. But when they confronted her at school, the daughter revealed that she was being bullied and forced to buy lunch for the bully and a friend who couldn't afford it. The parent's wife was upset, thinking this approach would damage their relationship with the daughter, and the daughter is now scared of retaliation and losing her friend. But what they didn't realize was the underlying reason for the daughter's actions. The daughter was being bullied and felt she had no choice but to steal to help her friend. Instead of addressing the root cause, the parent escalated the situation by involving law enforcement, which led to the daughter feeling scared and isolated. I think the parent's approach was too harsh. While it's important to teach consequences, using the police in this situation might have been overkill. It could have made the daughter feel like she's the one in trouble, even though she was acting out of necessity. The parent's wife suggested talking to the daughter first, which makes sense because communication is key. If the parent had talked to the daughter, they might have found out about the bullying earlier and could have addressed it more effectively. By involving the police, the parent not only scared the daughter but also potentially put her in a worse situation with the bully. The daughter is now worried about retaliation and losing a friend, which adds to her stress. This could lead to a breakdown in trust between the parent and child, which the wife was concerned about. In the future, it would have been better for the parent to approach the situation with understanding and support. They could have talked to the daughter about why she was taking the money, addressed the bullying, and worked together to find a solution. This way, the daughter would feel supported instead of punished, which could have strengthened their relationship and helped the daughter feel more comfortable coming to her parents for help in the future. So, considering all this, I think the parent did the wrong thing by calling the police without understanding the full situation. It led to negative consequences for the daughter and strained the family relationship.
